item.title: Russia's negotiator on Ukraine rejects option of territorial swaps with Kyiv, TASS reports
item.description:
MOSCOW, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Russia sees no possibility of exchanging territory with Ukraine as part of any peace deal, Vladimir Medinsky, Moscow's chief negotiator in peace negotiations, was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS on Wednesday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi.

Medinsky and Ukrainian negotiators had earlier reported some progress in the talks that ended on Wednesday, but US mediators said there was a lack of trust between the warring sides and differences remained on issues including territory.

item.title: Yemenis in Sanaa mourn dozens killed in strike blamed on Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Large crowds gathered in the Yemeni capital Sanaa on Wednesday to mourn the deaths of dozens of people, nearly half of them children, killed last week in strikes blamed on Saudi Arabia.

Mourners prayed at the city's Mosque of the People -- formerly the Saleh Mosque, but renamed by the Iran-backed Houthis after they took over the capital -- and chanted "Death to America! Death to Israel!" according to an AFP photographer present.

item.title: Egyptian court postpones retrial of independent news site's editor
item.description:
CAIRO, Nov 11 (Reuters) - An Egyptian court on Wednesday postponed until November 18 a retrial of the editor-in-chief of Mada Masr, a prominent independent news site, on charges of publishing false news and running an unlicensed website, the site said.

Human rights groups see the Mada Masr case as a litmus test of whether independent journalism can survive in Egypt, the Arab world's most populous country.

item.title: Hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, UK and Ireland in latest disruption
item.description:
By Alvise Armellini and Giuseppe Fonte

ROME, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after around 6,300 of them received bomb warnings, the latest in a series of threats and cyberattacks around Europe againstsupermarkets, blood banks, air traffic and broadcasters.

Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland said many of their schools received a similar email threat from abroad but it was classed as a hoax and did not disrupt classes.

item.title: COP31 leaders try out new sales pitch for climate action: do it for the economy
item.description:
By Ezgi Erkoyun and Valerie Volcovici

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Leaders at the COP31 summit in Turkey are trying out a new sales pitch for climate action that is tailored to the times: do it to bolster the economy and bring down the cost of living.

The message, being repeated in the hallways and on the plenary stage of the annual UN conference, reflects efforts by organizers to capture the attention of governments wrestling with crises that have pushed global warming down the list of priorities.

item.title: Russian negotiator reports some progress after Ukraine talks, sees no EU role in process for now
item.description:
MOSCOW, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Russia's chief negotiator at Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi said on Wednesday after their conclusion that mutual understanding had been achieved on some issues but not on others, and that more negotiations would take place.

VladimirMedinsky, in remarks broadcast on Russian state television, said that a new potentialfuture European security framework had been a central theme in the two-day talks.

item.title: Baltic nations, Finland issue overnight drone warnings as Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes
item.description:
By Andrius Sytas and Jekaterina Golubkova

VILNIUS, Nov 11 (Reuters) - NATO scrambled jets overnight after at least four drones strayed into the airspace of the Baltic states during Ukrainian strikes on Russia, officials said on Wednesday, triggering brief alerts to citizens of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to seek shelter.

Ukrainian military drones straying into the airspace of Finland and the Baltics this year have fuelled concern that the Ukraine war is spilling into NATO countries that border Russia and its ally Belarus.

item.title: Turkey’s banking watchdog chief submits resignation amid fund scandal
item.description: Turkey’s government is facing growing criticism over regulators’ failure to prevent a fund scandal involving more than $20 billion.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine say some progress made at talks, US cites a lack of trust
item.description:
By Roula Rouhana

ABU DHABI, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Russian and Ukrainian negotiators reported some progress in two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi that ended on Wednesday, but US mediators said there was a lack of trust between the warring sides and differences remained on issues including territory.

In their first peace talks for nine months, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a major release of prisoners of war, but there was little else in the way of concrete announcements after the US-brokered meetings.

item.title: Egypt’s independent press fights to survive as Mada Masr editor returns to court
item.description:
GIZA, Egypt, Nov 10 (Reuters) - An old villa, tucked away among mango and lemon trees in the back streets of Giza, once resounded with the clatter of keyboards and the chatter of people around its two long meeting tables but has now fallen silent.

Orderedby a court to close last month, Egypt's best-known independent news site, Mada Masr, has shuttered the villa as it awaits an appeal. Editor-in-chief Lina Attalah faces a separate case this week that could land her in prison.

item.title: Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country, security chief says
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Iran will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country and there will be consequences in the event of any new US strikes on the Islamic Republic, Iranian security chiefMohsen Rezaei said in televised remarks.

Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.

item.title: Israeli fire kills seven, including a father and son, in Gaza, medics say
item.description:
CAIRO, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Israeli forces killed at least seven Palestinians, including a father and his 13-year-old son, in the Gaza Strip on Tuesday, local health officials said.

Medics said Fadi Rajab and his son Abubakr were killed in an airstrike that hit the roof of a displacement shelter in the Zeitoun neighbourhood in Gaza City. A third Palestinian was killed in an Israeli airstrike near a school in Gaza City's Daraj neighbourhood, health officials added.

The Israeli military said it struck militants in both areas, without giving further details.

item.title: Iran designates Argentina's navy and air force as 'terrorist organizations'
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Tehran has designated Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations," Iran's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday, in a reciprocal move following Buenos Aires' designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist entity in April.

Argentina had designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, following a push from US President Donald Trump's administration for allies to do so.

item.title: War, conflict must not distract from climate action, leaders warn COP31
item.description:
By Tuvan Gumrukcu and Valerie Volcovici

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 11 (Reuters) - Wars and trade disputes should not be allowed to distract the world from its struggle to combat global warming, the leaders of Brazil and Turkey told the COP31 climate conference on Wednesday.

The comments on the third day of the annual UN summit came at the start of back-to-back speeches by world leaders that are meant to pave the way for negotiators to find a fresh deal to advance the international fight against climate change.

item.title: Barenboim orchestra spreads 'message of peace' in Berlin
item.description:
More than 25 years since its founding by star conductor Daniel Barenboim, the West-Eastern Divan Orchestra's mission to foster dialogue in the Middle East endures -- including among its own members. 

"Our message of peace must be louder than ever," Barenboim, who formed the ensemble alongside US-Palestinian intellectual Edward Said in 1999, told AFP ahead of a week-long festival celebrating the organisation in Berlin.

item.title: US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, sources say
item.description:
By David Lawder and Kanishka Singh

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after Iranian threats against his life, two people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

The New York Times first reported the move. A senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month that Iranian plots against US personnel and American citizens had reached an advanced stage.

item.title: Egypt court postpones hearing in case against prominent journalist
item.description:
A Cairo court on Wednesday postponed the retrial of the editor-in-chief of independent news outlet Mada Masr until next week to consider a defence request seeking the recusal of the judge, the outlet said.

The prosecution of Lina Attalah, one of Egypt's most prominent independent journalists, has drawn criticism from the United Nations, media watchdogs and rights groups, who say it could deal a final blow to one of the last remaining independent voices in Egypt's tightly controlled media landscape.
